items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: We played a battle of music the first night against Earl Hines.

ctx.x: we were staying at the Grand Hotel, and me and Chu tried to walk to the Grand Terrace for the rehearsal, you know... Man, we started... Those walks in Chicago are long, baby, believe me. Every block is like four blocks everywhere else. And we walked... We were at 51st and South Parkway, and we had to go to Oakwood Boulevard, that's 39th and Oakwood Boulevard. Well, we was stopping in every place we could find to stop in. Man, my balls were froze!

We got there and rehearsed, and things turned out real good. We did the sound... We played a battle of music the first night against Earl Hines. Tore him up, baby. Tore his group up. I'll tell you, it was so bad, that when you get... They had those jitneys in Chicago. When you'd get in the jitney, like I used to get in the jitney to go back up to the Grand Hotel, you'd hear like the cab driver talking to some people, saying, "Yeah, that band from New York, I don't know what kind of horns they got, but they really…

The band was a good band, really, and it stayed good until we came back. You know, we made the hit with "Christopher Columbus." I never did get no singing credits on that, but that was part of my tune, too, you know; because of the brass parts, you know. Another one of the things...heh-heh...
